cities.base: City centre near Trinity/Temple Bar for the first night, or near the airport for the last night since day 6 is a long drive in.
cities.name: Dublin

cities.base: Dingle town itself, small enough to walk, and the natural start for Slea Head and the Conor Pass.
cities.name: Dingle

cities.base: Day trip stop on the Dublin-Galway drive.
cities.name: Cliffs of Moher

cities.base: Drive-over from Dingle, combined with Slea Head day.
cities.name: Conor Pass

places.name: Trinity College / Grafton Street / Temple Bar
places.note: Don't fight jet lag with a big itinerary, just walk this loop and eat well.

places.name: Kilmainham Gaol
places.note: Books ahead and sells out; fits the arrival evening or a late last morning, don't force it into a driving day.

places.name: Cliffs of Moher
places.note: Go early, by 11am it's a car park with a view.

places.name: Kylemore Abbey
places.note: Pretty, overpriced for what it is, go for the walk not the building.

places.name: Sky Road, Clifden
places.note: Best in late afternoon light.

places.name: Slea Head Drive
places.note: The beehive huts and Dunquin Pier are the actual reason to come to Dingle, don't rush it.

places.name: Conor Pass
places.note: Narrow and closes in bad weather, check conditions the morning of.

places.name: Dingle town evening
places.note: Fish and chips or a pub with music, no fixed cost, €15-25 a head.

places.name: Trinity College and the Book of Kells
places.note: Long Room is genuinely worth it, the Book of Kells exhibit itself is a crowded shuffle past a single case. Book a timed slot online or the queue eats your morning.

places.name: Grafton Street
places.note: Pedestrianised, buskers, decent for a jet lagged shuffle between Trinity and St Stephen's Green. Not a destination on its own.

places.name: Temple Bar
places.note: The pub itself and the surrounding streets are priced for tourists and packed with stag parties. Have one pint for the photo, then walk five minutes to somewhere with locals in it.

places.name: Kilmainham Gaol
places.note: Guided tour only, tells the 1916 story straight, no filler. Sells out days ahead in summer, book online before you land.

places.name: Guinness Storehouse
places.note: Skip on a one-night stay. Seven floors of brand museum for a pint at the top, the queue and price aren't worth it when you have one evening in Dublin and better pubs everywhere.

places.name: St Stephen's Green
places.note: Free public park, good for shaking off jet lag with a slow lap. Nothing to plan around, just pass through.

places.name: National Gallery of Ireland
places.note: Free entry, small enough to do properly in an hour. Good rainy-afternoon fallback, not essential if the weather's fine.

places.name: Leo Burdock
places.note: Old-school fish and chips takeaway, no seating. Fine for a quick lunch near Christ Church, don't build a meal plan around it.

places.name: The Brazen Head
places.note: Claims to be Dublin's oldest pub, decent stew and trad music sessions most nights. Touristy but the food and atmosphere both deliver, better than most of Temple Bar.

places.name: Christ Church Cathedral
places.note: Medieval crypt is the actual highlight, older than most of what's upstairs. Worth a stop if you're already walking between Temple Bar and Kilmainham, not worth a detour on its own.

places.name: Howth Cliff Walk
places.note: DART train from city centre, about 30 minutes each way. Only makes sense if your last day flight is late afternoon or later, otherwise it eats the whole morning you need for the airport.

places.name: The Fumbally
places.note: Big airy cafe, good coffee and a real breakfast, mostly locals. A better start to the day than anything in Temple Bar.

places.name: Dingle Town Harbour and Main Street
places.note: Small enough to cover on foot in under an hour, colorful shopfronts, harbor with the resident dolphin boat tours. Good for a wander before or after dinner.

places.name: Dick Mack's
places.note: Former hardware store turned pub, still has the leather and shoe fittings on the walls. Stout, not always live music, but the atmosphere is real, not staged for tourists.

places.name: An Droichead Beag
places.note: Reliable trad music most nights, small and packed in high season. Get there before 9pm if you want to sit rather than stand at the back.

places.name: Out of the Blue
places.note: Seafood only, no menu printed until the day's catch comes in, no chips even. Small, book ahead in summer. Not cheap but the fish is the actual reason to eat here.

places.name: Murphy's Ice Cream
places.note: Irish sea salt and brown bread flavors, made in Dingle. Touristy but the ice cream is genuinely good, not just a photo stop.

places.name: The Fish Box
places.note: Casual fish and chips or chowder, faster and cheaper than the sit-down seafood places. Good lunch option between drives.

places.name: Dingle Distillery
places.note: Small distillery tour and tasting, gin and whiskey. Good rainy-day option, no reservation needed most days but check ahead in peak season.

places.name: Fahan Beehive Huts
places.note: Clochans, stone beehive dwellings from possibly early medieval times, small entry fee to a farmer's field. One of several such sites along Slea Head, this one is the easiest to pull into.

places.name: Dunquin Pier
places.note: Steep zigzag pier cut into the cliff, used in Ryan's Daughter. Short stop but the drop and the color of the water make it worth the five minutes down.

places.name: Gallarus Oratory
places.note: Dry stone church, roughly 1200 years old, still watertight without mortar. Small visitor center, short walk to the structure itself.

places.name: Blasket Islands Visitor Centre
places.note: Tells the story of the Blasket Islanders who left in 1953, good views out to the islands themselves. Worth it for context on Slea Head Drive, and a solid rainy-day fallback since it's indoors.

places.name: Mount Brandon via Faha
places.note: Ireland's second highest peak, roughly 12km round trip, 750m elevation gain, 5-6 hours. Only worth it in decent weather and only if you have a spare day, it does not fit into the Slea Head/Conor Pass day. Skip if the itinerary is already tight.

places.name: Cliffs of Moher Visitor Centre
places.note: Built into the hillside so it does not block the view, has the toilets, cafe and exhibition. Fine to skip the exhibition itself and just use it as a base.

places.name: O'Brien's Tower
places.note: The high point of the walk north from the visitor centre, small extra fee to climb it. The view is basically the same from the path just below, only climb it if it's not crowded.

places.name: South Trail to Hag's Head
places.note: Same cliffs, a fraction of the people. If you have more than the standard two hours this is where to spend it, quieter and the views back at the main cliffs are better from here.

places.name: Doolin
places.note: Small village 10 minutes north, good lunch stop before or after the cliffs, known for traditional music pubs though that's more an evening thing than a driving-day stop.

places.name: Gus O'Connor's Pub, Doolin
places.note: Reliable pub lunch, seafood chowder is the move. Gets busy with tour buses at peak lunch hours.

places.name: The Burren
places.note: Limestone karst landscape you drive through en route between the Cliffs and Galway or Dingle side trips, worth a short stop and photo even without a full detour.

places.name: Poulnabrone Dolmen
places.note: Portal tomb around 5,000 years old, right off the R480. Five minute stop, free, no gate or ticket, just pull in.

places.name: Kilfenora Cathedral and High Crosses
places.note: Small ruined cathedral with carved high crosses, low key stop on the way inland from the cliffs. Not worth a special trip but easy to fold in.

places.name: Aillwee Cave
places.note: Show cave in the Burren, guided walk through passages. Fine if you have kids or a rain backup, skippable if you're tight on time, it's a bit of a production for what it is.

places.name: Cliffs of Moher Cruise from Doolin
places.note: Boat out from Doolin pier gives you the cliffs from the water, genuinely a different and better view than the top for scale. Weather dependent and adds real time to what's meant to be a stop, not a full day.

places.name: Farm/sheepdog demonstration tours near Moher
places.note: Skip. Advertised heavily to the same crowd doing the cliffs, but it eats into the tight 5-6 hour window this stop is supposed to fit into on a driving day, and it's generic across half of rural Ireland.

places.name: Lahinch Beach
places.note: Surf beach just south of the cliffs, good for a walk or watching surfers if you want to stretch your legs before the drive continues. Not a swimming beach unless you're used to cold Atlantic water.

places.name: Sky Road
places.note: Loop drive out of Clifden with views over Clifden Bay and the offshore islands. Best in late afternoon light, a couple of pullouts to stop the car.

places.name: Kylemore Abbey
places.note: Pretty lakeside setting, the building tour itself is thin for the price. Walled Victorian garden a 15 minute shuttle ride away adds 45 min and is the better half of the visit.

places.name: Diamond Hill, Connemara National Park
places.note: Signed loop trail, 7km round trip, about 400m ascent, 2-2.5 hours if you do the full summit loop. Genuinely the best short hike in Connemara, views over the Twelve Bens and the coast. Skip if it's socked in with fog, you'll see nothing.

places.name: Derrigimlagh Bog Loop (Marconi Station / Alcock & Brown site)
places.note: Flat boardwalk loop across blanket bog past the ruins of Marconi's transatlantic wireless station and the spot where Alcock and Brown crash-landed after the first transatlantic flight. Odd, quiet, free, and nobody stops here.

places.name: Clifden town
places.note: The one real town on the loop, good spot for a coffee or lunch stop and a walk down the main street. Not a destination in itself, a waypoint.

places.name: Mannin Bay / Coral Beach
places.note: Small beach made of bleached coralline algae, not actual coral. Turquoise water on a sunny day, five minutes off the Sky Road loop. Worth a quick stop, not a whole detour.

places.name: Lough Inagh Valley drive
places.note: Quiet valley road running between the Twelve Bens and the Maumturk Mountains, lake on one side. No stops as such, just a scenic alternative route back toward Galway instead of retracing the N59.

places.name: Clifden Castle ruins
places.note: Roofless 19th century manor ruin on a headland outside town, short walk in from a small car park. Free, uncrowded, decent coastal views, easy to combine with the Sky Road.

places.name: Kylemore Abbey full house and craft shop tour
places.note: The gift shop and chocolate shop draw big coach crowds and add nothing. Do the grounds and garden, skip lingering in the retail end.

places.name: Oceans Alive Boat Trip, Cleggan
places.note: Seal-watching and coastal boat trip out of Cleggan harbour, weather dependent and needs advance booking. Nice if you have slack in the day but it will not fit comfortably alongside Sky Road and Kylemore in one loop, this is a trade-off, not an add-on.

places.name: Lunch in Letterfrack or Clifden
places.note: No standout destination restaurant on this loop, just budget a proper sit-down lunch break in one of the two villages, either before or after Kylemore. Simple pub food, chowder, sandwiches.

places.name: Aasleagh Falls
places.note: Small waterfall on the Erriff River right by the road near Leenaun, at the head of Killary Fjord. Worth the five minute stop if you're routing back via Leenaun rather than a special trip on its own.

outings.why: The reason to break up the Dublin-Galway drive, but go early because by 11am it's a car park with a view.
outings.name: Cliffs of Moher stop

outings.why: A full day out and back from Galway; Kylemore is pretty but overpriced, go for the walk not the building, and time Sky Road for late afternoon light.
outings.name: Connemara loop: Sky Road and Kylemore Abbey

outings.why: The actual reason to come to Dingle: beehive huts, Dunquin Pier, don't rush it.
outings.name: Slea Head Drive

outings.why: A narrow mountain pass that closes in bad weather, check conditions the morning of, don't treat it as a fallback if the day is already tight.
outings.name: Conor Pass drive-over
outings.fallback: Skip if conditions are bad; not worth forcing.

destination.name: Ireland
destination.pitch: Dublin as bookends and the west as the point: a real driving trip through the Cliffs, Connemara, and Dingle, not a bus tour.
destination.caveat: This whole trip lives or dies on a rental car and your comfort driving narrow roads on the left, and the long transfer days eat into anything else you'd want to do. Put together for you just now from what I know, rather than checked against today's opening times. Worth confirming anything you're pinning the trip on.

because.city: Dublin's Trinity/Grafton Street/Temple Bar core is walkable in an evening.
because.nature: The Cliffs of Moher, Connemara, and Slea Head Drive are the actual coastline, not a postcard of it.
because.culture: Kilmainham Gaol and Dublin's Georgian core give you the history bookend without needing a full day for it.
because.exploration: Sky Road and the Conor Pass reward just driving somewhere for the view.
